knowledge.text: Jointly adding an 'observed-without-goal = exhausted' rewording of the exploration principle plus a single-pass Search Strategy section (no immediate return to a just-observed location; no restart of a completed numbered sequence while another untried location remains; open closed containers before judging them empty) did not uniformly reduce repeated sweeps. On 'put a cellphone in shelf' (train:0005), 'put some newspaper on sofa' (train:0006) and 'put a pencil in desk' (train:0007) the Candidate executed more actions than its verified Parent counterpart (44 vs 30; 50 vs 41; 14 vs 10) and re-entered drawer sequences it had already observed empty (Q6:14, Q6:23, Q6:32; Q8:7, Q8:9), although the Parent also revisited observed-empty drawers (P6:8); all six sides still succeeded. Across the batch no pair regressed from Parent-success to Candidate-failure and action counts were equal in five pairs. The joint guidance was therefore not uniformly adhered to, and its intended cycling reduction is not established from these pairs; the principle rewording and the Search Strategy section are not separable from each other here.

On 'look at statue under the desklamp' (train:0004) the Candidate completed the task in 3 actions versus the Parent's 27: the Parent swept shelves 1-9, then opened drawers 1-3, then restarted the shelf sequence (P5:16) before reaching dresser 1 (P5:25), took the statue (P5:26) and used the desklamp (P5:27), whereas the Candidate went directly to dresser 1 (Q5:1), took the statue (Q5:2) and used the desklamp there (Q5:3). This is a large material asymmetry consistent with the edit's discouragement of restarting a completed numbered sweep, but the Candidate's initial choice of dresser 1 is not uniquely determined by the guidance (which constrains revisits rather than which location type to try first), so the whole reduction cannot be attributed to the edit; both sides succeeded.

Where the Parent already followed a direct route, the added search guidance produced no observed detour or container-handling regression: on 'put a soapbar in garbagecan' and 'put some statue on coffeetable' the Parent and Candidate used identical action sequences and equal action counts (4 vs 4; 16 vs 16), including opening closed drawers before judging them empty in train:0009 (P10:2, Q10:2), and all succeeded.

In an examine/look-under-desklamp task where the target (cd) was taken at a location without a desklamp (desk 1), the Candidate went from the first searched surface to the next untried location and used the desklamp there (Q3:4 shelf 1, Q3:5 shelf 2, Q3:6 use desklamp), whereas the Parent inserted a return to the acquisition location desk 1 (P3:5) between shelf 1 and shelf 2 before using the desklamp (P3:6, P3:7). Both succeeded, with the Candidate one action shorter (6 vs 7). This single-step local difference is consistent with the added examine-specific guidance against returning to a desklamp-less/recently-observed location while untried locations remain, but its small size limits causal inference.

The added examine-in-light desklamp section did produce a behavior difference from the un-edited Parent in one observed examine pair, train:0002 (look at cd under the desklamp): whereas the Candidate went from shelf 1 (Q3:4) straight to shelf 2 (Q3:5) and used the desklamp (Q3:6), the Parent returned to desk 1 (P3:5) — whose observation then showed only an alarmclock and a keychain, no desklamp — between shelf 1 (P3:4) and shelf 2 (P3:6) before using the desklamp (P3:7), giving 7 vs 6 actions with both runs successful. This divergence matches the examine-specific clause against returning to the desklamp-less location where the goal object had been acquired. In the other observed examine pairs, where no desklamp was present where the object was taken, Parent and Candidate behaved identically (take the object, then navigate to the desklamp and use it immediately) with equal action counts (train:0000 and train:0001: 4 vs 4; train:0003: 4 vs 4). Where a desklamp was visible at the location where the object was taken (train:0004), both Parent (P5:26, P5:27) and Candidate (Q5:2, Q5:3) used it immediately without relocating the object. Thus the only observed paired difference is the Candidate's one-step-shorter route in train:0002, and both agents succeeded in every pair.
